# Implementation

## Changed behavior

The intake validator now explicitly selects format version before validating the rest of an order. Omitted `formatVersion` and numeric `1` continue to use the original version 1 fields. Numeric `2` uses the partner format. Other values, including strings and null, are invalid.

Version 2 accepts the existing `id` and `customerId` rules, plus `amount.decimal`, optional `amount.currency`, and optional `shipOn`. Decimal text is converted exactly to integer cents, must be within 1 through 1,000,000 cents, and is not rounded or clamped. Omitted currency defaults to USD; a present currency must be exactly `USD`.

Version 2 `shipOn`, when present, must be `{ year, month, day }` with integer components for a real Gregorian date in 2000-2099. It is normalized to the existing `YYYY-MM-DD` string. When the entire version 2 date is omitted, the parser uses the call's trusted `context.receivedOn`.

All accepted orders still save and return only the canonical fields: `id`, `customerId`, `amountCents`, `currency`, `shipOn`, and `receivedOn`.

## Affected call paths

`submitOrder` and each `importOrders` row now pass `IntakeContext` into `parseOrder` so version 2 date defaulting uses the host-provided batch or request date. The storage path in `saveOrder` is unchanged: it receives canonical `OrderInput`, checks duplicates with `repository.get`, writes through `repository.save`, and maps repository failures to `storage_unavailable`.

Batch summaries continue to read only successful 201 row bodies, so version 2 rows contribute normalized integer cents and canonical date strings only after a save succeeds.

## Justified deviations

No new test files were added because the project has no test runner script. Validation was performed with focused runtime checks against a workspace-local compiled build and then the temporary build was removed.

## Remaining limitations

The implementation follows the documented scope: it does not add storage migration, damaged-record validation, retries, concurrency control, clock reads, currency conversion, or all-or-nothing batch behavior.
